visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 consistently places the correct open-top box variables and equations in context, while Lesson 2 repeatedly uses generic or misleading visuals such as closed boxes and an incorrect decreasing graph for S(x) instead of the U-shaped objective with a minimum.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have absent gate specs and absent plan JSON, so neither shows any functioning checkpoints or input-accepting questions.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 provides a coherent, speakable narration with no raw LaTeX or major garbling aside from a minor 'iron-cloud' misphrase, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript/narration available and therefore fails the narration-quality dimension.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 at least provides narration from which sync issues could be inferred, while Lesson 1 has no transcript or timing data at all, making it entirely impossible to verify any narration-visual alignment.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly derives the volume constraint, surface-area function, substitution, derivative, optimal side length 4 m, and minimum area 48 m² with a generally clear explanation, while Lesson 1 has no available teaching content to verify or learn from.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has larger, more legible typography, cleaner centered compositions, and a consistent polished illustrated style, whereas Lesson 1 often uses tiny text, sparse off-balance layouts, and comparatively plain diagrams with excessive empty space.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner. Although Lesson 1 strongly wins visual accuracy because its diagrams better match the open-top box setup, Lesson 2 wins most other dimensions, including very high-confidence wins in concept accuracy, narration quality, and polish, plus a lower-confidence sync advantage. The interactivity dimension is a tie because neither lesson provides functioning checkpoints or input-accepting interactions. Given that Lesson 2 has verified correct mathematical content and coherent narration while Lesson 1 lacks available transcript/teaching content in several judged areas, the weighted verdict favors Lesson 2 despite Lesson 1's visual advantage.
